purpose: personal account of testing AI automation on certificate design and hosting infrastructure

required_facts.fact: Alexey ran a two-day workshop in Berlin and needed certificates, including design, HTML/CSS conversion, PDF generation, and hosting.
required_facts.evidence: Source lines 1-5: workshop and certificate task are stated.

required_facts.fact: Several design approaches with Claude and Gemini produced inconsistent results and required manual intervention.
required_facts.evidence: Source lines 10-14: design experiment outcome is described.

required_facts.fact: The first design approach used ChatGPT for a certificate and background image, then Claude for HTML/CSS recreation.
required_facts.evidence: Source lines 18-26: first approach and tools are specified.

required_facts.fact: Alexey spent about 40 minutes iterating on spacing, alignment, and placement through review and new instructions.
required_facts.evidence: Source lines 28-32: manual feedback loop and duration are stated.

required_facts.fact: A creator-and-judge experiment used Claude to generate designs and Gemini Flash to evaluate similarity.
required_facts.evidence: Source lines 34-48: two-model feedback setup is described.

required_facts.fact: Claude sometimes discarded earlier work, and Gemini overestimated similarity, rating clearly different results around 8/10.
required_facts.evidence: Source lines 53-63: discarded design and inaccurate ratings are documented.

required_facts.fact: Claude Opus 4.6 analyzed the reference accurately, but a 44-iteration background run still failed to converge.
required_facts.evidence: Source lines 65-89: Opus experiment and non-convergence are stated.

required_facts.fact: The final design used the first approach with Claude iterating on Alexey's own feedback.
required_facts.evidence: Source lines 91-100: design result and manual-control conclusion are given.

required_facts.fact: Certificate hosting required S3, CloudFront, HTTPS, DNS, and configuration work and was usually expected to take several hours.
required_facts.evidence: Source lines 104-112: infrastructure context and normal effort are described.

required_facts.fact: Claude Code configured hosting through S3, Cloudflare, GoDaddy DNS, CloudFront, and HTTPS in about ten minutes.
required_facts.evidence: Source lines 114-116: access, actions, and setup duration are stated.

author_attribution: Attribute experiments, timings, model behavior, and conclusions to Alexey; preserve the contrast between manual design feedback and reliable infrastructure automation.
